articles.headline: GTA VI gamers beware — experts warn of a 1300% rise in phishing scams ahead of official launch date
keyFacts: Cybersecurity experts report a 1,300% increase in phishing emails using GTA VI as a lure to steal credentials.
Scammers are targeting corporate employees with fake pre-order offers and workplace benefits to bypass security systems.
KnowBe4 recommends that organizations implement layered defense strategies and train employees to recognize and report suspicious GTA-themed communications.
body: - A 1,300% surge in gaming-related phishing emails has been detected, with interest in GTA VI cited as the driving force
- 42.4% of all phishing email attempts at the end of October 2026 were GTA-related impersonation attempts
- Cybercriminals are using fake GTA VI pre-order offers to fool employees into handing over credentials for “workplace benefits”

Organizations are being urged to crack down on GTA VI-related emails and communications, following a striking uptick in phishing emails related to the upcoming video game. Following an increase of 1,300%, gaming-related phishing emails appear to be big business for scammers right now, with GTA VI the lure in the majority of cases.

Fake workplace bonuses, employee benefits, and QR codes holding “discounts” are all part of this wave of corporate phishing attacks, with 35% of similar attacks targeting the UK. Only the US, with 47% of attacks, has attracted more attention from the GTA VI scammers.
While security filtering software should be updated, employees should be vigilant, and made aware of the personal and corporate risks of falling for the dual attack strategy.
GTA-themed corporate phishing
The attempts to fool would-be victims with one eye on the release date of the most anticipated video game of all time rely on what is being termed “GTA-themed phishing.”

Two main waves are being employed: Wave 1, the mass-market email lure that is designed to overwhelm detection provisions and draw victims to anonymous landing pages with fake Rockstar Games branding, and Wave 2.

This second phrase is a smarter approach, targeting enterprise systems over the weekend, offering free or discounted pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6. It claims to be from the employer and relies on artificial urgency (e.g. the first 250 employees, expires in 48 hours, etc.) to fool recipients.
Once hooked in, the targets are redirected to fraudulent online casinos, and have their credentials harvested.

Dual-wave attack

These “dual-wave… hype-driven attacks” are designed to exploit the targets as much as possible. With this in mind, cybersecurity advice outfit KnowBe4 is recommending what is described as a “layered defense strategy.”

This includes training employees to recognize lures such as fake HR perks, and understanding their correct context – legitimate perks appear on company intranets, rather than being sent as unsolicited messages that include external links.

They note: “To ensure these targeted corporate lures bypass perimeter defenses, attackers combine psychological manipulation with a multi-layered technical evasion strategy. Rather than spoofing existing brands, threat actors register look-alike vendor domains that allow their emails to cleanly pass SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication checks. Once inside the inbox, the messages evade traditional image-based scanners by rendering QR codes entirely out of Unicode text block characters or HTML tables.“

So, stronger internal messaging, such as reminding teams that company benefits don’t rely on artificial urgency or QR codes is recommended. Limiting employees’ ability to use QR codes and minimize “quishing” where the device shift strategy – which bypasses corporate security measures – is also a smart precaution.

articles.headline: RJ Luis Jr., protected by a court order, makes his LSU debut amid NCAA and SEC objections
keyFacts: RJ Luis Jr. made his LSU basketball debut following a court-issued temporary injunction against the NCAA and SEC.
The NCAA and SEC argue Luis is ineligible because he entered the NBA draft and signed contracts with professional teams.
LSU President Wade Rousse stated the university will comply with the court order despite the SEC calling the decision deeply concerning.
body: BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — RJ Luis Jr., who briefly trained with two NBA teams and was added to LSU's roster this week over objections from the NCAA and the Southeastern Conference, checked in to an enthusiastic ovation during the first half of the 25th-ranked Tigers' tilt with Louisiana-Monroe on Wednesday night.
After entering the game with 12:05 left in the first half, Luis grabbed a rebound and later drew a loud roar of approval when he hit a 3.

A Louisiana state district court judge in Baton Rouge made it possible for Luis to play when issued a temporary injunction against the NCAA and the SEC, which have argued that the 2025 Big East Player of the Year is ineligible because he chose to leave St. John's to enter the NBA draft, never withdrew from the draft as required to return to college, and briefly was under contract with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics.

Luis' lawyers, Elliot Abrams of Raleigh, North Carolina, and Tony Clayton of Port Allen, Louisiana, have argued that because Luis never appeared in an NBA game, he is no more of a professional than dozens of players who were granted waivers by the NCAA after having played in pro leagues overseas.

LSU President Wade Rousse released a statement on Tuesday saying the university intended to comply with the judge's ruling, which temporarily barred the NCAA and SEC from declaring Luis ineligible or punishing LSU for allowing Luis to play.
“LSU is committed to compliance with NCAA and SEC rules, but it is equally committed to obeying the orders of Louisiana’s courts,” Rousse said.
The SEC called LSU’s decision “deeply concerning and disappointing.”

“LSU’s decision today to rely on its own interpretation of the court’s order to justify its actions is inconsistent with the expectations and responsibilities of membership in the Southeastern Conference,” the league said in a statement. “The conference will continue to uphold and defend the standards and policies established by its member universities.”
Luis joined LSU days after a victory over then-No. 14 Gonzaga that improved LSU to 4-0 and helped the Tigers climb into the AP Top 25 for the first time since the 2022 season.

LSU coach Will Wade, now in the first season of his second stint with the Tigers, also was LSU's coach in 2022, after which he was fired after the NCAA determined he had committed recruiting violations. Wade was found to have offered players or their families financial inducements that were not permitted at the time, and to have not cooperated with NCAA investigators.

Wade returned to coaching with McNeese State for the 2023-24 season, was hired by N.C. State in 2025 and then hired back to LSU last spring, several months after the former athletic director who had fired him had been ousted.

articles.headline: Elon Musk says record spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'
keyFacts: Elon Musk stated he felt foolish after spending $446 million on Republican campaigns during the US midterm elections.
Musk clarified he is not part of the Maga movement and does not support blind adherence to Republican policies.
Democrats gained control of the Senate and House despite Musk's significant financial contributions to Republican candidates.
body: - Published
Elon Musk said on Wednesday that he felt "pretty foolish" about the record sum he spent on the US midterm elections, following sweeping Republican defeats.
The Tesla and SpaceX CEO was the campaign's top individual donor, giving $446m (Â£339m) to support President Donald Trump's party, particularly in Texas where many of Musk's firms are based.
Musk, who had backed Trump's second White House bid, also said he was "not Maga" - the Make America Great Again movement associated with the president.
Democrats won control of the Senate and House, while Texas, Ohio and other states swung away from Trump, who has faced pressure over the impact his policies have had on the cost of living.
Musk was speaking virtually at the New York Times DealBook Summit, an annual conference hosted in the city attended by major business and political leaders.
"I'm not Maga," Musk said, referring to the right-wing political movement.
He added: "I'm not sure what Maga means... if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don't have that."
Musk went on to say he did not see much for the money he had spent on the Republicans' campaign, though he added that it was likely that candidates would have fared worse without the spending.
One of the most striking midterms wins went to Democrat James Talarico, who beat Republican Ken Paxton for a US Senate seat in Texas.
According to BBC analysis, Musk had spent at least $45m in support of Paxton.
Texas is where key operations for Musk's car company Tesla and rocket and technology firm SpaceX are based.
Democrats have vowed greater scrutiny of tech companies, including over the roll out of controversial data centres.

articles.headline: NC Courage star Ashley Sanchez wins NWSL MVP after matching single-season goal record
keyFacts: North Carolina Courage winger Ashley Sanchez won the NWSL MVP award after matching the single-season goal record with 20 goals.
The NWSL announced individual end-of-year award winners including Rookie of the Year Jordynn Dudley and Goalkeeper of the Year Ann-Katrin Berger.
Award winners like Sanchez will now transition to national team duties or prepare for the NWSL Championship game this Saturday.
body: The annual NWSL end-of-year awards rang in another special event. The league rolled out the blue carpet in Washington, D.C., and kicked off NWSL Championship Week by handing out individual honors.

The Kansas City Current and the Washington Spirit will compete in the title game on Saturday, but first the league wrapped up regular-season business by giving players and coaches their individual accolades. Players, coaches, owners and general managers, and fans voted for the awards.
Here are the official winners:
2026 NWSL MVP

The finalists: Temwa Chawinga (Kansas City Current), Trinity Rodman (Washington Spirit), Ashley Sanchez (North Carolina Courage), Janine Sonis (Denver Summit FC) and Sophia Wilson (Portland Thorns FC)
The winner: Ashley Sanchez

The North Carolina Courage winger set a record for most goals scored (20) by an American in a single season. It matches a single-season record, previously set by Temwa Chawinga, and now Sanchez can add the MVP award in addition to her Golden Boot win. Her remarkable career year comes after eight years in the league, but it feels like just the beginning for the 27-year-old, who will now head off to national team camps with the U.S. women's national team for World Cup qualifiers.

"I think it's definitely not something that I was thinking was going to happen at the beginning of this year. I was just really focused on myself and how I could grow as a player and a person," Sanchez told media after the awards show.

"I mean, I was not expecting this whatsoever and I'm really proud of myself. The team I have around me, they've just made me a better player and a better person. And yeah, it's just been an incredible year for sure.'
Rookie of the Year
The finalists: Jordynn Dudley (Gotham FC), Kat Rader (Houston Dash) and Mimi Van Zanten (San Diego Wave FC)
The winner: Jordynn Dudley

This is now the third consecutive rookie award that's gone to a Gotham FC player. Forward Jordynn Dudley's four goals and three assists were a big boost during Gotham's NWSL Shield-winning run. Her unfortunate season-ending foot injury cut her season a few weeks short, but also showed that the squad missed her attacking efforts on the pitch.

"It really shows what Gotham and the club what they prioritize with development and getting good talent coming in, and yeah, I thought it could continue," Dudley said about winning another rookie award for Gotham.
"Honestly, I wasn't expecting it. I'm just glad my teammates helped me get here, and my coaches and the whole team and the staff. So I'm really thankful for that," she said.
Goalkeeper of the Year
The finalists: Ann-Katrin Berger (Gotham FC), Jane Campbell (Houston Dash) and Jordan Silkowitz (Bay FC)
The winner: Ann-Katrin Berger

The Gotham FC goalkeeper set a personal best with six NWSL clean sheets to start the season and had 10 shutouts by August. She's the first goalkeeper with 10 or more clean sheets in back-to-back seasons, and was a massive part of why the East Coast side was one of the best defenses of the year, conceding only 23 goals against opponents across 30 matches.
Defender of the Year
The finalists: Tierna Davidson (Gotham FC), Kate Del Fava (Utah Royals), Sarah Gorden (Angel City FC), Janine Sonis (Denver Summit FC) and Kennedy Wesley (San Diego Wave FC)
The winner: Janine Sonis

It's one thing to have a career year, but to have a significant season for an inaugural club at a newer position is another thing altogether. Denver Summit defender Janine Sonis joined her home-state club from Racing Louisville, where she spent a half season moving from an attacking role to outside back. The 32-year-old scored 12 goals and delivered eight assists for the Summit as the group pushed for a playoff spot all the way to Decision Day.

"I feel really honored to just have won this award alongside the players that were nominated. There's incredible, like, world-class players in that category, and I think I just have so much respect for the position and the difficulty that comes with that position and being world-class there. I'm really honored to have won, but to be among them is just as special," Sonis said.
Midfielder of the Year
The finalists: Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current), Kenza Dali (San Diego Wave FC), Jaelin Howell (Gotham FC), Rose Lavelle (Gotham FC) and Mina Tanaka (Utah Royals)
The winner: Croix Bethune

The Kansas City Current will compete in the NWSL Championship on Saturday, and they'll have the midfielder of the year with them. Croix Bethune won the award in her rookie season back in 2024, and now has her second just two seasons later.

"A lot of blessings, a lot of hard work and dedication. I mean, this is coming off a meniscus tear, so setting goals, manifesting them, and it feels great making history," Bethune said after winning her award.
Bethune broke the all-time single-season assists record when she provided 11 assists to her teammates this year and four goals. This included a spectacular recent free-kick goal in the semifinal.
But her award honors her regular-season efforts, and now she's looking ahead to Saturday.

"The biggest thing is the environment itself, not necessarily me. And the environment that I walked into is still very positive, very energetic, very happy. My name is on the award, but there are 20 other people on my team that helped me get this award, so kudos to them," she said.
Coach of the Year
The finalists: Juan Carlos Amorós (Gotham FC), Jimmy Coenraets (Utah Royals) and Jonas Eidevall (San Diego Wave FC)
The winner: Jimmy Coenraets

The Utah Royals are one of the best stories of the season after their big turnaround from a lower-table team to the playoffs. Head coach Coenraets was honored for the efforts and credited the award to his team and the club.

"I think if I look back at the season, yes, we've achieved sporting success. But above all, I think there has been a very clear way of doing things, a very clear way of playing for a special reason, and showing up every single game in the same way. That was a goal in the beginning of the season. We said very loud we want to be competitive. I think we've been competitive all season. I think incredibly proud of this group to just do that and go beyond it," he said.

articles.headline: Trump minimizes Jensen Huang scandal: ‘We have to take care of our geniuses’
keyFacts: President Donald Trump said he might have briefly discussed former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a dinner in China.
Trump defended Huang after his forced exit over extramarital affairs, stating that the nation must take care of its geniuses.
Nvidia does not plan to reinstate Huang as CEO, according to the company's chairman.
body: President Donald Trump said he “might” have informally raised former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a dinner in China after Huang was forced out of the company he founded following a series of extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy.
“I might have referred to it just briefly because it’s such a tragedy,” Trump told Fox News in Shenzhen, China. “He’s such a brilliant man.”

During an interview on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on Thursday local time before meetings with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin , in addition to a separate sit-down of all three men, Trump reiterated his desire for Huang to be returned to Nvidia.

“Some people can’t be replaced,” he said. “He was 10 years ahead. The Blackwell chip is 10 years ahead of any other chip, and the interesting thing is it can’t be copied, you know, because of the level of complexity.”
Of Huang, Trump added that “we have to take care of our geniuses” because “we don’t have that many of them.”

“When we have brilliant people like Jensen, we can’t say, ‘Oh, you know, he did this,'” he said. “We have to take care. You know, I helped Elon [Musk] a lot in my first term. I helped him a lot. He was in big trouble, and now we have a guy that’s sending up rockets and landing them. You know, nobody’s ever seen like what happened the other day, where the ship comes in and lands safely, and they save billions of dollars, and it’s the way of the future.”

Trump remained adamant that he has no intention to ask Xi not to spy on the United States and sidestepped questions regarding his openness to easing export controls on the chips like those sold by Nvidia.
NVIDIA DOES NOT PLAN TO REINSTATE JENSEN HUANG AS CEO, CHAIRMAN SAYS
“They’ll ask me to stop doing it, and I don’t know if I’d do that,” he concluded.

Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed International, whose Singapore-based company acted as a pass-through company to avoid restrictions on selling Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China.

articles.headline: Elon Musk tries to explain what’s going on with Ukraine and Starlink
keyFacts: Elon Musk stated at the DealBook Summit that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is lying about the use of the Starshield system.
Musk claimed Starlink is a civilian system and should not be used for offensive military drone strikes.
Musk asserted that offensive military actions must be conducted through the government-controlled Starshield system rather than his private service.
body: Elon Musk said Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is lying about disruptions to Starshield in Ukraine and that he’s trying to misuse SpaceX’s consumer service, Starlink, for military purposes. Musk made the comments at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday as he tried to explain the conflict following weeks of back and forth between Zelenskyy, Musk, and the US government.
Elon Musk tries to explain what’s going on with Ukraine and Starlink
The SpaceX CEO claims that Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is ‘lying’ about using Starshield.

“From the beginning, I’ve said that Starlink is a civilian system,” Musk said. “It is not meant to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people. If you want to do that, you need to do Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the US government. But do not ask me as a private individual to make kill decisions.”

Musk also said that “if they want to do something that’s an offensive military action, it needs to be the Starshield system where the kill decision is that of the War Department, perhaps ultimately the president, and not mine.”

The interviewer, Andrew Ross Sorkin, said that President Zelenskyy refers to the system as Starshield and is claiming that is the system that was slowed down. “That’s false,” Musk said, claiming that Zelenskyy is “not always truthful.”
Sorkin asked, “So when President Zelenskyy talks about using Starshield, he is not using Starshield, or he’s lying?”
“He is lying,” Musk said. “What he is actually saying is he wants to use Starlink for offensive military operations.”

And according to reporters at the big game, the crowds were similar to what you might see on Black Friday, as thousands of fans tried to get their hands on exclusive GTA-themed merchandise.

articles.headline: Trump downplays US outages and Nvidia security concerns in remarks before China summit – live
keyFacts: Donald Trump told Fox News that recent widespread US computer outages were individual events caused by companies installing new equipment.
US intelligence warned Trump that Nvidia's chief executive had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, the New York Times reported.
Donald Trump will reportedly meet one-on-one with Vladimir Putin during his Asia summit, the Guardian reported.
body: Trump downplays outages and Nvidia security concerns in remarks before China summit

Speaking with Fox news, Donald Trump said he wasn’t worried about multiple outages this week affecting Microsoft, US banks, United Airlines computers, the National Security Agency’s internal comms network, Apple services and the national air traffic control system.
“They’re all individual events. These are big companies. They’re putting in new equipment and things happen when you put in new equipment. And these are all individual things,” he said.
When asked whether he raised the issue of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman suspected of being a spy for China with Xi, Trump said he “might’ve referred to it just briefly”
“Because it’s such a tragedy. It’s a tragedy. He’s such a brilliant man ... we have to take care of our geniuses,” Trump said of Huang.

Of Alice Huang, Jensen Huang’s affair partner, the president mused: “I haven’t heard that she was a spy. She was a business woman who bought chips. Who knows if they were bought right or wrong. But I can tell you we allow them to buy. We want to make money.”

However, according to a report by the New York Times, Trump was briefed aboard Air Force One in May en route to China that the US intelligence showed that that Nvidia’s chief executive was in a relationship with a woman thought to be a Chinese spy.
Trump also shrugged off the Fox reporter’s question about whether he would confront China over spying allegations.
“We spy on them too”, he said. “I think we spy better than they do.”
Donald Trump says he's open to deal making with Democrats
Donald Trump, who repeatedly prophesied an apocalyptic future if Democrats regained control of Congress, has changed his tune, telling Fox News the next two years will be “unbelievably productive.”
He suggested he would be liberal with his veto power, but also open to cutting deals across the party line.

“They’ll send me a bill on health care and I’ll say no way and I’ll veto it. And then, they’ll call me and we’ll sit down. That’s what I do,” Trump said on Wednesday. “Politics is a nasty game. They won.”
Donald Trump asked about one-on-one with Vladimir Putin amid the Russian-Ukraine war
Donald Trump will reportedly meet one-on-one with Vladimir Putin, the prime minister of Russia, during his Asia summit.
When asked by Fox News if he mentioned the bilateral meeting to Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump appeared to sidestep the question.

“They got to get along,” Trump replied, referring to Zelenskyy and Putin, whose countries remain at war. “If I were president, if the election weren’t rigged, that war would’ve never happened,” he added, repeating a baseless election fraud theory.

Since February 2022, when Putin ordered the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by Russian forces, nearly 18,000 citizens have been killed and 58,000 injured, according to estimates from the United Nations.

Trump then offered a wildly inflated death toll for the conflict, claiming that “probably two million people, mostly soldiers, are dead.” In fact, more than 400,000 Russians have been killed fighting in Ukraine since Russia’s full-scale invasion, according to leaked data from the state statistics agency, Rosstat. In July, the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated that between 125,000 and 150,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed.

“It’s a shame. It’s so sad. It doesn’t affect us,” Trump told Fox News. He noted that the US has sold military equipment to the European Union, which provides it to Ukrainian forces, in contrast to what he framed as handouts from his predecessor Joe Biden’s administration. Trump repeated his false claim that “Biden gave $350m in cash away” to Ukraine. In fact, the US Congress provided about half that sum, $174bn, in arms to Ukraine, and the Biden administration gave Ukraine a $20 billion loan to be repaid with frozen Russian assets.
“I guess you could say, we make a lot of money with that. I don’t care. I don’t want that,” Trump said.
Trump downplays outages and Nvidia security concerns in remarks before China summit

Speaking with Fox news, Donald Trump said he wasn’t worried about multiple outages this week affecting Microsoft, US banks, United Airlines computers, the National Security Agency’s internal comms network, Apple services and the national air traffic control system.
“They’re all individual events. These are big companies. They’re putting in new equipment and things happen when you put in new equipment. And these are all individual things,” he said.
When asked whether he raised the issue of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman suspected of being a spy for China with Xi, Trump said he “might’ve referred to it just briefly”
“Because it’s such a tragedy. It’s a tragedy. He’s such a brilliant man ... we have to take care of our geniuses,” Trump said of Huang.

Of Alice Huang, Jensen Huang’s affair partner, the president mused: “I haven’t heard that she was a spy. She was a business woman who bought chips. Who knows if they were bought right or wrong. But I can tell you we allow them to buy. We want to make money.”

However, according to a report by the New York Times, Trump was briefed aboard Air Force One in May en route to China that the US intelligence showed that that Nvidia’s chief executive was in a relationship with a woman thought to be a Chinese spy.
Trump also shrugged off the Fox reporter’s question about whether he would confront China over spying allegations.
“We spy on them too”, he said. “I think we spy better than they do.”
US admits ‘substantial’ change to extradition request translation for leftist activist
Timothy Pratt

US authorities have admitted altering the translation of an extradition request for James “Fergie” Chambers from English into Spanish, attributing violent and illegal actions to the wealthy activist and philanthropist that were not in the original.

Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.

In a notification sent to Spain’s ministry of justice, the US Department of Justice (DoJ) cites three of the examples of legally significant alterations revealed in the Guardian’s reporting on the issue, calling them “substantial [and] inadvertent”.

The notification arrived to defense attorneys, the prosecutor and a three-judge panel on Tuesday as the judges were deliberating whether to grant the US extradition request, leading the defense team to file a motion calling for a halt in the proceedings and a new translation.

The US has now admitted to three of the alterations detailed in the Guardian’s reporting, and calls the fourth “an acceptable translation”. One of them involves introducing the word “fire” in describing late 2023 protests against Elbit, an Israeli weapons manufacturer. Two of the three charges in the criminal complaint against Chambers are related to the protests – where nothing was set on fire.
Construction on Trump's triumphal arch continues to be barred
A federal judge has extended the construction ban on Trump’s triumphal arch, in the latest setback for the president’s capital makeover agenda.

The Memorial Circle-slated arch was conceived as a visual ode to the nation’s 250th year of independence, among several other beautification projects, but its construction has been halted amid litigation.

In February, a trio of veterans and an architectural historian filed a legal challenge against the Trump administration, saying the arch would obstruct the symbolic view between the Arlington national cemetery and the Lincoln memorial, a line of sight meant to represent a unified nation post civil war, according to the complaint.

Members of the Kennedy family have since joined the legal action, arguing the arch would cast a shadow on former president John F. Kennedy and other relatives’s graves, which US district judge Tanya Chutkan cited in her extension.
The order is set to expire on 3 December, or before if the court rules on pending motions for a preliminary injunction.
'Foolish': Elon Musk reflects on massive midterm political spending
Elon Muskpoured nearly half a billion dollars into the midterms, as he sought to tilt competitive races in favor of Republican candidates.
In the end, Democrats claimed victory across the country, including in Texas where Musk’s aerospace and rocket company SpaceX is headquartered.
“It certainly shows that American elections are not just about money,” Musk said on Wednesday at the New York Times DealBook Summit according to the paper.
“If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.”
Trump's transportation secretary blames contractor for nationwide ground stop

As legislators press for more answers on last week’s outage that caused thousands of flights to be halted, snarling travel plans nationwide and globally, US transportation secretary Sean Duffy has pointed a finger at contractor L3Harris.
Transportation officials have said the aerospace and defense company was updating copper wire lines to fiber in Arkansas, when a newly installed router flooded the network.
“This was not identified quick enough. It was not isolated quick enough,” Duffy said Wednesday on digital media outlet 2WAY’s The Morning Meeting. “We’re working on how to remedy that right now.”
A spokesperson for the government contractor could not be immediately reached for a response.
The official cause of the router malfunction remains unknown.

Duffy’s agency has been modernizing an outdated air traffic control system, switching copper lines to fiber and wireless, and analog systems to digital. Last Friday’s ground stop order was the second advisory of its type, since the 9/11 attacks.
In its wake, Duffy has also tore into Democratic lawmakers and previous administrations over funding to the aging system.
US defense secretary Pete Hegseth boasted about the capture of Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro during his first trip to Caracas, the country’s capital.

“Exactly one year ago today … [Maduro] stood on a stage not too far from here and yelled mockingly, ‘Come and get me!’” Hegseth said in front of the recently reopened US embassy on Wednesday, before adding sarcastically: “Well, we answered that call.”
“The reality is that … January 3 is the day that will go down in history as a day of liberation for Venezuela,” Hegseth claimed, although Maduro’s allies continue to hold power with US support.
More from The Guardian’s Latin American correspondent Tom Phillips.

Jim O’Neill will not undergo a confirmation hearing on Wednesday to head the National Science Foundation (NSF) because he “did not do enough to stand up for science” in his previous position, said Bill Cassidy, a Republican from Louisiana who is chair of the Senate committee on health, education, labor and pensions.

This ends O’Neill’s run for the top US scientific organization, an embattled independent federal agency that has seen major budget cuts and grant freezes under the Trump administration. The next NSF nominee will face a Democratic-led Senate.

O’Neill served as acting director of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) from August 2025 to February 2026. In that role, he failed to push back against “irresponsible decisions and statements from Secretary Kennedy”, Cassidy said in opening remarks before the committee on Wednesday, hours before O’Neill was slated to appear.

“His role in the firing of Susan Monarez raised further concerns about the independent judgment he would bring to NSF,” Cassidy added, saying that several members of the committee had concerns about those lapses. Cassidy said that he likes O’Neill personally, “but this time requires leadership and fortitude in standing up for what is right”.

O’Neill also served as deputy secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) from June 2025 to February 2026, a time during which HHS slashed recommendations for routine childhood immunizations.

The White House did not pull O’Neill’s nomination. But Cassidy noted that the White House did yank the nomination of Heidi Overton for commissioner of the US Food and Drug Administration, saying she lacked the votes to pass confirmation – which Cassidy said was “pretty odd”.
“I think she would’ve had the votes,” Cassidy said. He noted that anti-abortion senators “sought reassurances from the administration” about Overton’s stances against abortion.
“They chose not to make such commitments and ultimately withdrew Dr Overton,” Cassidy said.
Incoming House Democrats to attend private reception with Barack Obama - reports

Incoming House Democrats have been invited to a private reception today, organized by minority leader Hakeem Jeffries – who won the party’s nomination for speaker earlier. According to several reports, former president Barack Obama will be the event’s special guest.
The reception will take place away from Captiol Hill, and members-elect boarded buses earlier, according to the notice that various outlets reported.

House Democrats have nominated current minority leader Hakeem Jeffries as their candidate for speaker in the next Congress. Jeffries received 251 yes votes of 262 cast, and 11 members voted no on his nomination. He faced no challengers but it will lead to a full chamber vote in the new year when Democrats are in the majority. Jeffries is poised to be the first Black speaker in US history.

Meanwhile, Chuck Schumer, the current Senate minority leader facing a challenge for the majority leader position from Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen, continued to express confidence he would prevail. “I will be elected majority leader. I’m confident we have the votes,” he told reporters today. In that case, he was asked, should Van Hollen give up his bid? “That’s going to be up to him,” Schumer said. “I think what we all want to do is roll up our sleeves together, everybody, and deliver for the American people. That’s what we’re focused on. That’s what we’re focused on.”

During a fiery House hearing, Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, defended his decision to take a government plane to attend a college football game, while thousands of flights had been cancelled and the airspace closed during the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) nationwide grounding over the weekend. “You want to bring up the fact that I took my family and my great nieces to an [Lousiana State University] game that was scheduled for weeks prior because I wanted to be a good uncle,” Mullin said, following questions from Congressman Bennie Thompson, the homeland security committee’s top Democrat. Mullin went further, and said that had he not traveled to the game it could have created “confusion” because he was due to meet Louisiana governor Jeff Landry. Mullin added that his absence might have shown “distrust that we’re not even willing to fly” after the FAA reopened the airspace.

Congressman Robert Garcia, the incoming chair of the House oversight committee, has sent 12 letters to members of Donald Trump’s family, current and former officials, and aides ordering them to preserve documents ahead of the sweeping inquiries that Democrats are set to launch in the new Congress. The document retention letters, were addressed to vice-president JD Vance, Eric Trump, Donald Trump Jr, Stephen Miller, the White House chief of staff, and his predecessor, Susie Wiles, among others. Garcia noted that the scope of the likely investigations will focus on alleged family corruption, misconduct at the Department of Homeland Security, and the justice department’s handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files.

In response, Will Scharf, the White House general counsel, hit back in a letter to all ranking committee members in the House and Senate, claiming that several of their requests“drip with an animus or pettiness revealing that the purpose of these letters is not legitimate oversight but to harass and aggrandize”. Scharf added that “although some of you may (or may not) become a Chair in the 120th Congress, that does not mean that requests from the 119th Congress carry over.” In the majority, Democrats have vowed to launch sweeping investigations into a variety of issues and officials when they have subpoena power.
White House hits back at requests for information of officials and aides

Will Scharf, the White House general counsel, has hit back at Democratic lawmakers who have requested information and documents from administration officials, aides and allies in recent weeks, as the party prepares to take the majority of both chambers in the new year.

This comes after Robert Garcia, the incoming chair of the House oversight committee, sent 12 letters to members of Donald Trump’s family, current and former officials, and allies ordering them to preserve documents ahead of the sweeping inquiries that Democrats are set to launch in the new Congress.

Scharf addressed a letter, first obtained by Politico, to all ranking committee members in the House and Senate, claiming that several of their requests “drip with an animus or pettiness revealing that the purpose of these letters is not legitimate oversight but to harass and aggrandize”.
Scharf added:

Your demands do not reflect a request of the House, Senate, or a committee to which that body’s oversight authority has been delegated. As a result, Ranking Member requests in the 119th Congress do not trigger any obligation to “accommodate[e]... the needs of the conflicting branches.” Although some of you may (or may not) become a Chair in the 120th Congress, that does not mean that requests from the 119th Congress carry over.
This, Scharf highlighted, “should not be surprising” to Democrats, noting the party took the “same position” in 2022, when they were relegated to the minority in the House.
In the majority, Democrats have vowed to launch sweeping investigations into a variety of issues and officials when they have subpoena power.
And in other news, from the basement of Capitol Hill …
Thomas Massie, the outgoing Republican congressman, shared pictures of his new office in the final weeks of the 119th Congress.

“It’s half a cubicle, but I have an extra seat for one staffer,” Massie said. “It’s traditional to kick non-returning members out of their offices early and ship them to this cubicle farm. The assumption is lame duck members just quit working … not me!”

A reminder that Massie lost his primary in May, after bucking with Donald Trump on several occasions. Earlier this month, Massie also launched a failed effort to impeach defense secretary Pete Hegseth, but his resolution was effectively killed when Republicans sent it to committee for further review. Democrats, however, have vowed to relaunch the attempt in the new year when they take the majority in both chambers.
One note, tomorrow’s meeting between Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen is set to last fewer than 60 minutes.
“No more than an hour” has been set aside for the historic summit between the three leaders, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media on Wednesday.

The US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, faces mounting questions over his handling of the Nvidia affair as Democratic lawmakers demand answers over his family firm’s vast stake in the tech company.

Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm Lutnick ran for decades before joining the Trump administration, held shares in Nvidia worth “hundreds of millions of dollars” while Lutnick made key decisions affecting the tech firm’s ability to operate, according to Democrats on three key congressional committees.

“The American people deserve to know: did the secretary of commerce seriously and perhaps irreversibly compromise US national security interests to make money for his adult children and Cantor Fitzgerald?” said Jamie Raskin of Maryland, Gregory Meeks of New York and Sydney Kamlager-Dove of California.
Cantor Fitzgerald insists it had “no role” in the Trump administration’s decisions about Nvidia.
But in a letter on Tuesday to Lutnick’s son Brandon, who now serves as chair of Cantor Fitzgerald, the trio of lawmakers demanded documents and records, including communications concerning Nvidia.

They said that they wanted to “understand whether any actions or decisions by Secretary Lutnick concerning export controls, enforcement measures, or national security policies may have been improperly influenced by Cantor Fitzgerald’s holdings or business interests”.
And responding to the nomination of Hakeem Jeffries to be the next – and first Black – House speaker, Chuck Schumer told reporters:

I’m so glad he was elected by such an overwhelming margin. He’s going to be a great speaker. It’s historic. I’ve known him from the very early days when he was even running for Congress, and I look forward to working with him together.
'I will be elected majority leader': Schumer expresses confidence he has the votes to beat Van Hollen
Chuck Schumer, the current Senate minority leader facing a challenge for majority leader from Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen, also expressed confidence he would get the position.
Asked by a reporter if he was concerned about his election, Schumer replied: “No. I will be elected majority leader. I’m confident we have the votes.”

In that case, he was asked, should Van Hollen give up his bid? “That’s going to be up to him,” Schumer said. “I think what we all want to do is roll up our sleeves together, everybody, and deliver for the American people. That’s what we’re focused on. That’s what we’re focused on.”

Trump criticized media coverage of the outages while attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China.
body: President Donald Trump softened his rhetoric regarding the spate of technological issues that have rattled the public during an interview while on his trip to Asia .

When asked what his message is to the public after outages at the likes of Microsoft, Chase Bank, and even the National Security Agency, which has spooked some people into stockpiling food and money, Trump told Fox News it would be “to relax.”
“Tell them to relax, everything’s good,” Trump said on Thursday local time in Shenzhen, China. “These are individual events.”

Trump had earlier downplayed concerns, saying that tech problems are part of “life” and happen “when you’re big and powerful” during a photo opportunity at his first stop in Manila, the Philippines, for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit.

But on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, Trump criticized the press coverage of the issues, arguing that if they had occurred during former President Joe Biden ‘s administration “nobody would have mentioned it.”

articles.headline: California faces horrifying budget hole as Xavier Becerra gets grim warning: ‘Dangerous stage’
keyFacts: Legislative analysts reported that California faces a projected $2 billion deficit next year that could reach $30 billion by 2030-31.
Analysts warned that the state relies heavily on capital gains taxes from an artificial intelligence stock market boom that could burst.
Analysts suggested $6 billion in budget solutions next year, while Democratic leaders pledged to prepare and strengthen state reserves.
body: California could face years of staggering deficits running into the tens of billions of dollars within five years if urgent budget repair is not carried out – and the AI boom goes bust.
While the outlook projects California will face a $2 billion shortfall for the upcoming fiscal year, it predicted the deficits are set to soar to at least $15 billion by 2028-29.
And in a worst-case scenario, the shortfall could be potentially as high as $30 billion by fiscal year 2030-31.

“The problem in the upcoming budget year is relatively small, but it grows to be fairly significant,” legislative analyst Gabe Petek said on Wednesday.
Analysts fear an AI bubble could burst the stock market, which is currently propping up the state’s finances with its capital gains tax revenue.
Advertisement
Analysts said lawmakers have to take that risk seriously.
“While the stock market’s recent run has been great for many investors and the state budget, it now appears to have advanced to a dangerous stage,” analysts wrote.
Petek added that the signs of a burst are there: “Every one of these indicators that we’re looking at is the highest they’ve ever been – except for at the peak of the dot-com bubble.”
Advertisement
Analysts suggested that the state make $6 billion in cuts or “budget solutions” next year to build up to a $4 billion cushion.
Democratic leaders in the state legislature quickly pledged on Wednesday to prepare for it.
“We will continue to strengthen our reserves and protect health care, food aid, emergency response and our schools,” Assembly Speaker Robert Rivas said in a statement.

“That’s how we keep costs steady and make every dollar count. Whatever comes next, California will be ready.”
Democrats pointed to the recently voter-approved Proposition 2, which lawmakers proposed to double the cap of the state’s rainy day fund.
The top lawmakers said they will look at moving more of any excess revenues into those reserves to prep for any downturn.
“The new administration will have to face reality. The stock market returning to more normal levels is a matter of when, not if,” Niello said in a statement.
“Otherwise, when the market eventually corrects, the consequences of today’s budget problems will catch up with us.”
Advertisement
Becerra, as the next governor, will have to provide an initial spending plan by Jan. 10. His spokesperson said in a statement that he “is hard at work preparing his first budget proposal.”
“He remains committed to delivering a responsible, balanced budget that protects the services Californians depend on and focuses on bringing down costs,” the spokesperson said.

Becerra, before the election, had said “everything should be on the table” when asked whether he would support a mileage-based tax to maintain California’s roads, with Republicans claiming the Democrat was intending to introduce one.
“He said, ‘everything’s on the table,’ and then he started arguing in favor of it,” Assemblymember Carl DeMaio told The Post. “He literally was making the argument for the mileage tax.”
The Becerra campaign has stated that he has not proposed a mileage tax. The Post reached out to Becerra’s spokesperson on whether any new taxes may be sought after in response to the budget outlook.

In late October, Becerra himself was asked by a reporter on the campaign trail regarding the state budget relying too heavily on the AI stock boom — and if California may need to see service cuts or tax increases.
Becerra simply responded that the government has to be “steady” even if the stock market is not.
“We’re not going to overspend. We’re going to make sure we’re fiscally prudent,” Becerra said.

articles.headline: Did Christopher Nolan Just Bring 4K Blu-Ray Discs Back to Stores?
keyFacts: Best Buy has resumed selling 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray discs after previously announcing it would cease all physical media sales in 2023.
The retailer is currently stocking copies of the film The Odyssey, which was filmed entirely on IMAX cameras and achieved high box office success.
Best Buy has not yet confirmed if it plans to expand its in-store inventory to include other 4K or standard Blu-ray titles.
body: Physical media lovers, take note: Best Buy has begun selling 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray discs in-store and online. If you’ve been paying attention, you’ll know how big a pivot this is for the electronics retailer. Back in 2023, the company announced it would cease all sales of DVDs and Blu-rays entirely.

Now, thanks to Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster phenom and Oscar frontrunner The Odyssey, which is the first-ever movie to be filmed entirely on IMAX cameras, the company is once again stocking its shelves with Blu-rays. Right now, you’ll find only copies of the Greek epic in store (with a small selection of other titles available for purchase directly through the retailer’s online store), and that makes sense considering how popular it was in theaters and how awesome it will look on big TVs at home.
But this move also raises the question: Will other 4K and standard Blu-rays be coming to Best Buy stores in the near future?
More from CNET
A Best Buy spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

When the retailer first announced it would be ditching DVD and Blu-ray sales, it cited the decades-long decline in physical media sales — which fell from its peak revenue benchmark of $16 billion in 2005 to less than $1 billion in 2024 — and planned to populate the store space with other tech-based products.

The Odyssey, the nearly 3-hour-long big-screen adaptation of Homer’s epic poem, follows King Odysseus (played by Matt Damon) as he leads his soldiers on a 10-year journey home after the Trojan War. It features a stacked slate of acting talent from Anne Hathaway and Tom Holland to Zendaya, Jon Bernthal and Charlize Theron, and earned $1.8 billion at the global box office.
Those details, along with the timing of the coming holiday shopping season, have apparently inspired Best Buy to change course.

It should be noted that physical media still has value for many people. In an era when movies and TV shows (purchased or otherwise) are suddenly pulled from streamers, the allure of owning titles on DVD and Blu-ray endures. Not to mention, 4K Blu-rays offer better picture quality than their compressed, streaming versions.

articles.headline: Why a trio of experts alleges Jeffrey Epstein did not die by suicide
keyFacts: Three experts released a report stating Jeffrey Epstein’s injuries are most consistent with homicidal strangulation rather than suicide, casting doubt on official rulings.
Epstein died in a New York jail in 2019 while awaiting trial on federal sex trafficking charges.
The experts alleged that investigators failed to identify the neck ligature and ignored unacknowledged back and neck bruising.
body: A trio of experts has released a report casting doubt on whether convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein died by suicide in his jail cell in 2019, as a medical examiner in the United States previously ruled.

In documents obtained by Al Jazeera and other media outlets, Michael Freeman, Anders Eriksson and Itiel Dror – a forensic scientist, a forensic pathologist and a cognitive scientist – said the injuries on Epstein’s body were “most consistent with homicidal strangulation”, not suicide.
“The pattern, distribution, and multitude of injuries are not explained by a suicidal hanging,” their report reads.
Instead, they suggest Epstein was first assaulted and then strangled, providing an alternative narrative to the medical examiner’s 2019 report.
The cause of Epstein’s death has long been a source of controversy and conspiracy theories.

A wealthy businessman, Epstein cultivated a range of high-profile relationships with leaders in politics, industry, academia and the arts. His network of contacts included US presidents Bill Clinton and Donald Trump.
Those connections have raised questions about whether there was a cover-up of Epstein’s crimes – or whether some of his associates knowingly turned a blind eye.

In 2008, Epstein pleaded guilty to the solicitation of a minor for sex as part of a plea deal that saw him serve 13 months behind bars. Later, in 2019, he was arrested on federal charges of sex trafficking, with prosecutors accusing him of having “sexually exploited and abused dozens of underage girls”.
He died in a New York City jail while awaiting trial.
A controversy over cause of death

Medical examiner Kristin Roman performed the autopsy on Epstein’s body. She and New York City’s Chief Medical Examiner Barbara Sampson ultimately ruled that the evidence pointed to a suicide by hanging.
Other experts have sided with their ruling, pointing out that, while the circumstances of Epstein’s death were unusual, they are not necessarily inconsistent with suicide.
But Epstein’s brother, Mark, has long doubted the medical examiner’s findings. He gave Freeman, an Oregon-based forensic scientist, access to the death records.
Freeman has consulted in trials where families have questioned the narratives put forward by law enforcement about how someone died, including in high-profile cases like the murder of George Floyd.
Eriksson, meanwhile, is a Sweden-based forensic pathologist who has researched issues like shaken baby syndrome, a controversial diagnosis used to prosecute some adults for abuse of young children.
He and Freeman worked alongside Dror, a cognitive scientist who studies biases in forensic science.
At the time of his death, Epstein was a well-known figure, and Dror said the investigators handling his case would have been subject to significant political pressure.
“It’s so obvious this played a critical role in the examination of the body,” Dror told Al Jazeera.

“There was at stake a lot of emotion, a lot of people involved, a lot of politics involved, so many factors. You can list them for an hour, and all of those interfered and biased and influenced what should be a scientific decision.”
Dror explained that he and his colleagues pored over photos and records related to Epstein’s death and concluded that the medical examiner had wrongly ruled it a suicide.
Points of concern raised
In their report, the trio noted a number of issues with the initial investigation.

The prison personnel who found Epstein’s body did not take any photos before moving it, for instance. Investigators also failed to identify the ligature, the object that was actually around Epstein’s neck, they said.

They allege that some avenues of investigation went unexplored. The prison guard who first came across Epstein’s body initially refused to be interviewed, according to the report, and the medical examiner who determined the case was a suicide was not allowed to visit the prison.
The report also disagrees with the medical examiner’s assessment of Epstein’s injuries.
Marks left by the ligature on Epstein’s neck, the researchers said, were not slanted in the way that would be expected if his body had been hanging from the bedpost in his cell.
They observed bruising on Epstein’s back, shoulder and neck that they said was not acknowledged in the medical examiner’s original statements.
Those injuries, their report said, are “most consistent with homicidal strangulation from behind, most likely using a narrow knotted fabric ligature”.

Freeman, Eriksson and Dror believe either that the prison guard who found Epstein was lying about finding his body hanging in the cell, or that the body was deliberately put into that position to make it seem like a suicide had taken place.

articles.headline: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit
keyFacts: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees to manage the company's transition toward an AI-first operational model.
Nadella stated the buyouts provide employees agency to choose between adapting to new AI-focused roles or leaving the company.
The company aims to reorganize workflows so that employees manage AI agents rather than performing traditional tasks directly.
body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff.

Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI.
The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the DealBook Summit.

“Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he explained.
For some people, “that reorganization and change is sort of hard, right?” he added, “but, I mean, it has to be done.”

He offered the example of the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. He said the team consists of just 11 developers who have mastered using AI to do their jobs. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.”

He believes that every employee will one day similarly become a manager of agents, rather than a person directly doing the work. “That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs.”

But Microsoft, as a 51-year-old company, didn’t grow up as an AI-first company. “So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?” he said. “It’s going to take a bit more time than anyone expects. And there is going to be in all of this, you know, people who may say, ‘Hey, I have some other choices I want to make.’”

When asked about this same topic — why ask 60,000 people to voluntarily resign — last week by Gergely Orosz on his The Pragmatic Engineer podcast, Nadella further explained, “We have created enormous anxiety in people sort of feeling that they don’t have control of their own destiny because the way we have talked about this AI revolution.”

He called out talk about the singularity (the hypothetical point at which AI surpasses human intelligence) and predictions that AI will take away all jobs. “All of that leads anyone who even wants to change to be sort of anxious … You have to sort of walk the hard walk of really making the structural changes, getting people slotted, giving them opportunity.”
In other words, the buyout was the message to employees: You can get with the new AI-first program, which will radically change your job, or you choose to get on with your life. Elsewhere.

articles.headline: Chinese web giant Tencent says new US GPU ban ‘sets everyone back in China’
keyFacts: Tencent president Martin Lau stated that new US regulations restricting GPU access will negatively impact the company's ability to train AI models in the short term.
Lau expects the restrictions to accelerate China's development of domestic supply chains and chips to meet future computing needs.
Tencent plans to maintain its international cloud services by working with partners and utilizing non-GPU resources despite the new US export limitations.
body: The USA’s new ban on Chinese companies remotely accessing GPUs will have short-term impact, but ultimately see China accelerate its development of domestic alternatives, according to Martin Lau, the president of Chinese web giant Tencent.
Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Lau said the new US regulation will have an “unfortunate” impact on Tencent’s business.

“It does set everyone back. It sets everyone back in China,” Lau said. “So everyone is actually having less advanced compute to work with, no matter when you actually started leasing or building capacities outside of China.”
He said the ban will impact Tencent’s ability to train models.
“Our training efficiency with Hy4 is actually very high,” he said. “When we look at the next version, it would take probably longer time for us to come up with the next version in the short run.”
“But over time, the domestic supply chain would actually come on board.”
Lau also thinks the bans won’t hamper Tencent’s ability to run inferencing workloads, because made-in-China chips “should be able to cover it.”

“And over the longer run, we believe all Chinese players would actually have to rely on domestic supply chains and domestic chips, which we see the industry is progressing very fast,” he added. “With the latest restriction, we expect it to actually speed up even further, because all the development effort would actually have to be focused on speeding up the domestic supply chain.”

Tencent needs GPUs, and lots of them, because the 10 million users of its agentic assistant WorkBuddy are collectively consuming over 100 trillion tokens per day. Lau thinks WorkBuddy is on track to becoming a hit product, partly because many users are outside China.

Lau said Tencent can serve WorkBuddy customers outside China because the service can operate with different models, and the company thinks it can find third parties to provide the necessary inferencing services without the new US bans creating a problem.
But Lau said that GPU rentals and other cloud services, which are also growing strongly, may be impacted.

“In terms of cloud, if it is non-GPU related, we can actually build capacities ourselves outside of China,” he said. “I think there is still a lot of such opportunities because our cloud service is actually very cost competitive. When it comes to GPU, then unfortunately, we cannot actually offer high-end GPU anymore. We may be able to work with some partners in different places.”

Tencent doesn’t break out revenue for its cloud services, but said they rose by 35 percent year-on-year, well ahead of the company’s overall eight percent growth. Marketing services also grew strongly, by 19 percent, thanks in part to new AI-powered systems that improve ad targeting.
The company’s WeChat and Weixin messaging platforms continued to grow, adding 35 million accounts to exiting the quarter with 1.44 billion monthly active users.
One Tencent biz that went backwards was its international gaming unit, which saw revenue fall nine percent.

Chief strategy officer James Mitchell said that slowdown wasn’t caused by the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. “ I think that in fairness, the slowdown for us predated the run-up to GTA VI,” he said, before predicting that Tencent’s existing and future “evergreen games” should help to turn things around.
GPUs might help, too.
“The game environment globally is one where the rate of innovation has slowed somewhat, and now with AI, there’s opportunities to re-accelerate innovation,” he said. ®

articles.headline: GTA 6 Officially Cuts A Controversial Franchise Feature After 25 Years
keyFacts: Grand Theft Auto 6 will not include hirable sex workers as NPCs, ending a feature present in the franchise for 25 years.
Rockstar stated that the game's features were chosen to support the specific story of the protagonists and the intended gameplay systems.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is scheduled for release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X on November 19.
body: You can do anything you want in a Grand Theft Auto game, but the franchise has historically been defined by a handful of specific mechanics. Steal a car. Shoot pedestrians. And for better or worse, soliciting a prostitute. Grand Theft Auto 6, however, is an unusually realistic game that tells a humane story about a couple, and those shifts in approach are reflected in the game's actions.

Prostitutes made their debut as NPCs in 2001 with the release of Grand Theft Auto 3. These characters, which appeared on the game's streets at night, could be solicited by the player for $100. Though the encounters were explicit in nature, the animations at the time only showed the vehicle bouncing suggestively.

The arguably tame mechanic became infamous for two primary reasons. Many fans approach GTA as a chaos simulator, so players sometimes target sex workers indiscriminately. It became a running joke, for lack of a better word, for GTA fans to sleep with and immediately kill the women they hired. Once dead, the NPCs would drop the money the player used to hire them.

Another major source of the feature's infamy was Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas' Hot Coffee incident. In short, Rockstar designed a mini-game that allowed CJ, the protagonist, to have sex with a prostitute. Unlike GTA 3, this minigame didn't leave things to the imagination — the characters could be seen bent over and going at it. Rockstar pulled the minigame out of San Andreas for the official release, but the feature was still hidden in the game's files. In 2005, when San Andreas was ported to PC, modders found the minigame and released it to the public under the name Hot Coffee.
Are the controversial NPCs in GTA 6?

Many years later, after much legal rigmarole and multiple new games, Hot Coffee has defined the public's view of GTA as a franchise. Yet despite all the headaches Hot Coffee caused Rockstar, the developer nonetheless continued to include sex workers through Grand Theft Auto 5. In that game, the player purchase services by sex workers that were, in some cases, animated more scandalously than those in Hot Coffee. Rockstar's addition of a first-person view further heightened the intensity of these encounters. GTA V was also the first game to include a crass caricature of trans sex workers available for hire — a fact that was heavily decried by queer fans who felt Rockstar was punching down.

Now, 25 years after their original inclusion, hirable sex workers are not making a return in GTA 6. Given the game's enormous number of encounters, a sex worker could still appear somewhere in GTA 6. As a type of highly visible NPC, however, prostitutes are gone.

Rockstar did not immediately respond to a request for comment. However, a representative told Shacknews that “GTAVI is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run. While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in VI has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon — things like wanted system, the radio, robberies and car theft."

The explanation makes sense given GTA 6's realism and heightened gore. Critics have already noted in their reviews that, for the first time ever, breaking the law or harming NPCs sometimes inspires guilt. Rockstar's justification has still disappointed fans who consider prostitutes a key pillar of the franchise. Most people don't seem to mind and appear content with being able to visit strip clubs.

"Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTAVI, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia's story," Rockstar's statement continued.
Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

articles.headline: Anthropic’s early birds are getting very rich
keyFacts: Anthropic, developer of the chatbot Claude, is expected to go public at a valuation of over $1 trillion.
Executives, employees, and early investors stand to benefit most from the company going public.
Direct public ownership of Anthropic stock is expected to begin tomorrow at 9 a.m.
body: Anthropic signage at the Morgan Stanley headquarters in New York on November 18, 2026. | Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images
This story appeared in Today, Explained, a daily newsletter that helps you understand the most compelling news and stories of the day. Subscribe here .
Americans have debated, derided, praised, and protested the frontier AI labs. But they’ve never been able to directly own a piece of one…until tomorrow at 9 am.

That’s when Anthropic, developer of the chatbot Claude, is expected to go public at a valuation of more than $1 trillion . That would immediately rank the almost-six-year-old lab among the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies — up there with the likes of Walmart and JPMorgan Chase.

It’s a major public test of what investors think Anthropic is worth, at a moment when a lot of people — policymakers, regulators, and technologists among them — are questioning the economic and social value of the AI industry. AI stocks have been shaky lately, and many of the new congressional Democrats have promised to take a tougher stance toward data centers and related technology.

But you wouldn’t know it from the hype around the IPO, which is on track to become one of the largest ever. Anthropic initially set a price range of $70 to $78 a share, then reportedly revised the offering at $83 per share as demand surged far beyond the number of shares available.

Investors are apparently betting that Anthropic has more growing to do. For ordinary buyers, that represents a chance to share in a company whose technology could cost us our jobs …if not our very existence on Earth . 💀
The biggest winners, however, will almost undoubtedly be the executives, employees, and early investors at Anthropic itself. The timing of the IPO helps with that.
Go a little deeper
View Link
Some of America’s most iconic companies went public very early in their lifecycles. (Think Apple, Amazon, and eBay, which all IPO-ed before they were five years old.)

But over the past two decades or so, many of America’s biggest businesses have instead grown in private. Between the early 2000s and 2025, the median age of a company at IPO doubled from six years in 2000 to 12 in 2025.

Analysts credit two main factors for these increasingly late-breaking IPOs. One is the fast-growing availability of private capital from venture funds, wealthy individuals, and other companies. Firms that once needed to go public to raise money to grow can now raise that money privately.

The other factor is the desire to maintain control over the company and its information: Private firms don’t have to file public financial reports or give public shareholders a vote on corporate matters.

But while that may be good for companies and their leaders, it’s not always or unambiguously great for the general public. Financial reports shed valuable light on how a business operates and where its risks lie, for instance.

There’s a financial downside for us normies, too. “The way I see it, the later a company goes public, the more of its growth gains accrue to private investors,” Brad Badertscher , a professor of accountancy at the University of Notre Dame who has studied IPO trends, said in an email to Vox.

Under this system, insiders like executives, employees, and early investors can nab shares at a low price while the company is still young and then benefit if its value goes up. Retail investors only join the party after much of that growth has already happened.

Of course, growth is never guaranteed. Early investors, private or public, also take on a lot of risk. And even now, several years in, new investors are still taking a substantial risk when they buy shares in Anthropic — a company that, in the grand scheme of recent IPOs, isn’t even that late to the process.

There’s the threat of greater regulation from a Democratic Congress. The fallout of the shake-up at Nvidia. The specter of a potential AI market crash (to say nothing about the aforementioned end of the world).
If would-be shareholders are bothered, however…you’d never know it! They’ve been waiting years to buy Anthropic stock, and they very much want in.

But you don’t have to be a master chef to turn out a great Thanksgiving feast (…or to feel confident in the kitchen, in general!). Buy a decent knife and stock your spice drawer. Set some small, manageable goals. And make your kitchen a fun place to be. It makes all the chopping go much faster.

articles.headline: GTA 6 Launch Causes Massive Spike in Traffic for Internet Provider Xfinity

body: Internet provider Xfinity has reported a massive spike in traffic on Xbox consoles for GTA 6's New Zealand launch.

Xfinity says it saw a jump in Xbox hardware traffic four times more than normal around the time GTA 6 became available in New Zealand. Although Xfinity provides its services in the United States, Xbox users were able to take advantage of a loophole that let them change their console's region to New Zealand, allowing them start playing the game early despite their actual geographic location. It's one of the only real notable advantages Xbox has had over PlayStation with this game, as Rockstar secured a marketing deal to advertise GTA 6 as playing best on PS5.

However, these hours of early access have proven to be very lucrative for Xbox players. As a result, tons of footage for the game has been circulating on social media all day long. Major content creators also took advantage of the New Zealand trick, resulting in record-breaking viewership across platforms like Twitch . As of this afternoon, Twitch reported that tens of millions of watch hours had already been accumulated.

Right now, we still don't know how many copies of GTA 6 have sold, but we'll likely hear something by the end of this week or very early next week, depending on how quickly Rockstar wants to boast. This is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all-time, after all, and the official numbers will likely be eyewatering.

From a critical perspective, GTA 6 has received nothing but praise. IGN gave the game a 10 for its impeccable attention to detail and unprecedented depth, but we weren't alone in that analysis.
